# onpager_service (Data Source)

Read one OnPager service through authorized configuration reads. Absence, ambiguity and denied reads are errors. Reads never modify configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onpager_team" "owner" {
  name = "Operations"
}

data "onpager_service" "example" {
  name = "Public API"
  # Optional: fail if the service is owned by a different team.
  team_id = data.onpager_team.owner.id
}

output "service_id" {
  value = data.onpager_service.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Stable OnPager UUID. Configure exactly one identity selector. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID; computed when another selector is configured.
- `name` (String) Exact case-sensitive name, preserving whitespace. Configure exactly one identity selector. Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes; use `id` for longer stored names. Computed when another selector is configured.
- `team_id` (String) Current owner team UUID. When configured, constrains expected ownership for either an `id` or `name` selector; it is not an identity selector. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID. Computed from the observed service when omitted.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Observed active state. Inactive objects remain readable; this data source never changes their state.

## Selection

Configure exactly one of `id` or `name`. Optional `team_id` verifies the
service's current owner for either selector; an ownership mismatch produces a
diagnostic. Without `team_id`, the current owner UUID is recorded in state.

Name matching is exact and case-sensitive and preserves surrounding whitespace.
Names are unique within the tenant, including inactive services. Name lookups
use exact server-side filters with `limit=2`; a configured `team_id` is combined
with `name` using AND. Zero matches, multiple matches or `has_more` produce a
diagnostic. The name is limited to 4096 UTF-8 bytes and the full JSON filter to
8192 bytes. UUID selection reads the service directly and bypasses these filter
limits.

The unique match is read directly by UUID before its metadata is returned.

## Read behavior

Reads service metadata and ownership, including inactive services. Missing
services, denied access, malformed responses and transport failures produce
diagnostics.

## Permissions

Requires `services.read` in the current owner team or at tenant scope for
personal tokens and service accounts. The team lookup in the example separately
requires `teams.read` for the selected team.
